media.caption: Ichiyōsai Kuniteru’s print arranges workers and equipment in two rows beneath repeated roof supports. NDL catalogues this impression as [1872]; MAFF dates a comparable impression 1873 without establishing the NDL copy’s date. The published depiction supports observation of its drawn arrangement, not a measured floor plan or a photograph of every shift. Individual identities, working hours and freedom remain unestablished; modern digitization date unstated.
notice: Find the two rows of workers and equipment and the passage between them.

media.creator: Ichiyōsai Kuniteru (Utagawa Kuniteru II), artist; Daikokuya Heikichi, publisher
media.place: Tomioka, Gunma, Japan, depicted workplace; catalogue publisher in Tokyo. No artist visit or measured room geometry established.
media.material: Color woodblock print (nishiki-e), three-sheet composition; modern digital reproduction
media.representedDate: An artistic representation of early Tomioka mill work. A particular shift, individual identities and the exact moment represented are unestablished; this is not a photographic exposure date or a measured survey.
media.relevance: Makes workers, equipment and a constructed workplace visible through a published representation. Training, employment conditions and enforcement require separately dated records rather than an inference from orderly composition.
